body.statement: For every valid input \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) with \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le r_{n,d,M}\), \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) returns \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) satisfying \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\subseteq\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) and moving each endpoint outward by at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\). Its bit-operation count is \(O\bigl([dL_n^3+(n+d)L_n^2\lceil\log_2(8M/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\rceil]b_{\mathrm{work}}^2\bigr)\), hence polynomial in \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(\log(1/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\). Consequently, its coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\) and its worst expected length is at most \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]+2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\).
body.justification: Outward interval arithmetic gives coverage monotonicity only after a valid exact-real score root and a score-to-root error modulus have been established.
body.gap: The current nonmonotone score has multiple roots and vanishing derivative, so the claimed uniform bisection and bit bound are not yet certified.
body.consumer: The intended consumer remains an auditable implementation for the \(n=9915,d=8196\) application.

obligation.what_is_open: A certified outward root enclosure and the claimed bit complexity for the actual statistical score equations.
obligation.obstruction: The coefficient and factorial magnitude envelope can be propagated by interval arithmetic, but endpoint error requires converting score error into root error. The stipulated score is nonmonotone and has zero derivative at \(\pm\sqrt2\); no retained bracket with a positive slope modulus is defined. Thus bisection is not certified and the frozen working-precision formula cannot yield the claimed uniform endpoint tolerance. The exact-real heavy score is also absent.
obligation.attempted: I propagated the banked coefficient bound \(6^{2K}\) through the declared \((en)^{8L_n}\) magnitude envelope and verified the deterministic inclusion, coverage-monotonicity, and length consequences of outward endpoint enclosures. The missing slope bound prevents completing the root and bit-count induction.
obligation.partial_result:
Suppose an exact-real interval \([L,U]\) has already been defined and interval
arithmetic returns \(\widetilde L\le L\le U\le\widetilde U\) with
\(L-\widetilde L\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\) and
\(\widetilde U-U\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\).  Then deterministically
\([L,U]\subseteq[\widetilde L,\widetilde U]\), coverage is monotone under
this inclusion, and
\[
 (\widetilde U-\widetilde L)-(U-L)\le2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}.
\]
The banked coefficient bound \(|g_{Kj}|\le6^{2K}\) with \(K\le L_n\) also
places polynomial/factorial intermediate magnitudes below the declared
\((en)^{8L_n}\) envelope after the frozen input-precision condition is used.
What is missing is a uniform outward enclosure for the roots: the stipulated
score is not monotone and its derivative can vanish, so no uniform
score-to-root error conversion or bisection count follows from the current
formula.
